licton_springs_kitchen_bath_remodel.heading: Kitchen and Bathroom Remodel in Licton Springs
licton_springs_kitchen_bath_remodel.text1: This Licton Springs project combines a compact kitchen and bathroom renovation where both rooms needed to do more with limited square footage. The work focused on layout, custom built-ins, storage, and finish details that make the spaces feel more open and useful.
licton_springs_kitchen_bath_remodel.text2: The kitchen uses blue lower cabinetry, warm wood uppers and trim, open shelving, bright counters, and a clean backsplash. A custom oak table and built-in bench create dining space without crowding the room. The bathroom was expanded into part of the hallway and a child’s bedroom, creating a larger full bath with a shower window and built-in shelving.
licton_springs_kitchen_bath_remodel.short2: Kitchen and Bathroom Remodel in Licton Springs

part1.small_heading: A compact kitchen designed to feel open, warm, and practical
part1.text2: This compact kitchen delivers impactful daily functionality. The remodel brings together blue lower cabinets, lighter wood upper cabinets, open shelving, a bright backsplash, and clean counters so the room feels layered without becoming visually overwhelming.
part1.text3: The contrast between the painted base cabinets and the warm wood details gives the kitchen personality, while the matching sink countertop and backsplash keep it feeling calm and usable.

part2.small_heading: A custom oak table and built-in bench solved the space problem
part2.text2: A custom oak table with a built-in bench solved the room’s tight dining-space challenge, creating a more efficient eating area directly within the kitchen.

part3.small_heading: Clean backsplash, open storage, and appliance zones sharpen the finish work
part3.text2: The stove wall, backsplash, and open shelving bring out this kitchen’s personality, and this section of backsplash still carries the blues from the lower cabinets.

part4.small_heading: The tiny bathroom was expanded into the hallway and kids’ bedroom
part4.text2: The original bathroom was a tiny room that needed to feel larger and become more functional. To make that happen, the remodel borrowed space from the hallway and part of a kids’ bedroom, allowing the finished bath to function as a true full bathroom while feeling far more spacious than before.
part4.text3: That extra space made room for a better layout and improved comfort.

part5.small_heading: A shower window helps the compact bath feel brighter and more open
part5.text2: A window within the shower brings valuable natural light into the small room. In a room this small, natural light becomes part of the design strategy because it keeps the enclosure from feeling boxed in.
part5.text3: The glass shower wall, vertical tile, and window placement work together to visually stretch the room and make the finished space feel cleaner and more open.

part6.small_heading: Built-in shelves made the enlarged bath more useful
part6.text2: Built-in shelving uses about a foot of former hallway space to add valuable storage without cluttering the bathroom.
part6.text3: That kind of decision is a good example of practical remodeling: small layout adjustments can dramatically improve storage, organization, and everyday usability in a compact bathroom.
